Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme request to publish customer story — sensitivity check

Jonas —

Thanks for the flag. Quick thoughts from GTM/legal liaison perspective:

- Do not approve verbatim right now. The draft includes a quote that references "zero downtime" which is inaccurate given the incident; that will look tone-deaf.
- Recommend two options to propose back to Acme:
  1) Short delay (4 weeks) until the post-mortem's key remediation items are in place and we can jointly approve language.
  2) Move forward but change the quote to focus on performance improvements (latency/cost) rather than absolute reliability, and include explicit language that the parties can review the quote before publishing.

From a contract/risk perspective, we should escalate to Legal for a quick read (I can loop them in) and offer Acme a courtesy review period. Also recommend offering a small marketing credit or extended pilot as a goodwill gesture to reduce churn risk and preserve the relationship.

If we go with option 2, we'll need Communications + Legal to sign off and make sure any performance numbers are mutually verified.

Happy to draft a reply to Acme proposing both options and asking for their preference. Approve me to send?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Marketing
Redwood Inference

From: rachel_kim@redwood.ai

Jonas / Marissa —

Adding CS perspective: Acme is fragile right now on account metrics — net retention for the robotics line dipped in July after the incident. They are absolutely sensitive to anything that looks like overselling. My recommendation: offer option 2 (edit + review) with a one-month embargo and give them final sign-off on the quote. Also offer a one-off credit (10% of next quarter invoice) or a free month of Dedicated capacity to sweeten the ask — that will help retention and makes us look collaborative.

If you approve, I can take point and propose the language below to Acme. Proposed reply (draft):

"Hi Alice — thanks for the draft and for the transparency. We're supportive of being featured, but given the recent operational event we suggest two paths: either a short, 4-week delay while we finalize remediation, or we proceed with an edited story that focuses on the deployment benefits (latency, cost savings) and explicitly allows Acme final review of any quote before publication. We're also happy to provide a one-month service credit as a goodwill gesture. Which option do you prefer?"

I can send this to Alice and copy Legal if you both approve.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
